source.author: cic
source.text: quo loco etiam atque etiam facite ut recordemini quae sit temeritas multitudinis, quae levitas propria Graecorum, quid in contione seditiosa valeat oratio.
source.text_original: quo loco etiam atque etiam facite ut recordemini quae sit temeritas multitudinis, quae levitas propria Graecorum, quid in contione seditiosa valeat oratio.
source.text_english: In this matter, take care again and again to remember what the recklessness of a mob is, what the fickleness that is characteristic of the Greeks is, and what power a seditious speech has in an assembly.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Doctissimi quique Graecorum, de quibus pro Flacco agens luculente Tullius ait: ingenita leuitas et erudita uanitas, regum suorum uel principum laudes accepta mercede dicebant.
reuse.text_original: Doctissimi quique Graecorum, de quibus pro Flacco agens luculente Tullius ait: ingenita leuitas et erudita uanitas, regum suorum uel principum laudes accepta mercede dicebant.
reuse.text_english: The most learned of the Greeks, concerning whom Cicero, speaking in defense of Flaccus, said most eloquently, innate frivolity and learned vanity, used to recite the praises of their kings or princes for payment received.
